sources.title: FFmpeg official download and release page
sources.version_commit: FFmpeg 9.0.2, latest stable at access; release date 2026-09-18
sources.locator: Releases; 9.0.2 library versions; release vs development-branch guidance
sources.observed_operation: Opened and read current official download/release page.
sources.condition_default_exception: The page distinguishes slow-moving stable release branches from more rapidly updated development, and says FFmpeg only provides source code while linking to separately built packages.
sources.applicability: Pin and verify the actual parser/runtime build; do not infer platform support from project name.

sources.title: ffprobe Documentation
sources.version_commit: Online FFmpeg documentation, live page accessed 2026-10-12; related current stable release S01
sources.locator: Description; -show_format, -show_streams, -show_error, -of json, -formats/-demuxers/-codecs; JSON optional-field behavior
sources.observed_operation: Opened the official manual; earlier read its description/options.
sources.condition_default_exception: The manual says a positive exit code occurs when input cannot be opened or recognized; JSON is machine-readable, optional invalid/non-applicable fields may be omitted under auto behavior.
sources.applicability: Technical metadata and diagnostics only; not a promise of successful playback or accurate duration.

sources.title: FFmpeg Formats Documentation
sources.version_commit: Online FFmpeg documentation, live page accessed 2026-10-12
sources.locator: Input options analyzeduration and duration_probesize; format_whitelist; probe defaults
sources.observed_operation: Opened documentation and reviewed probing behavior.
sources.condition_default_exception: analyzeduration is documented as defaulting to 5,000,000 microseconds; increasing it may improve detection but raises latency. Duration probes are not extended at all costs and extra probing can have a performance cost.
sources.applicability: Record probe limits and duration provenance; bounded metadata extraction needs explicit timeout/uncertain duration states.

sources.title: FFmpeg ffprobe source
sources.version_commit: FFmpeg tag n9.0.2
sources.locator: File header and imports; section definitions for format, streams, errors, and output writer; option/state tables
sources.observed_operation: Opened released source text at the pinned tag.
sources.condition_default_exception: Source identifies ffprobe as a media prober built on FFmpeg libraries and makes output sections/options explicit; supported sections vary with build and selected options.
sources.applicability: Evidence for a concrete metadata adapter and version-specific source review, not a live execution.

sources.title: FFmpeg FATE ffprobe tests
sources.version_commit: FFmpeg tag n9.0.2
sources.locator: Entire 23-line test recipe, especially ffprobe command and output-mode test targets
sources.observed_operation: Opened released FATE test recipe at the pinned tag.
sources.condition_default_exception: Tests create a deterministic short NUT test file with audio/video/metadata and assert compact, CSV, default, flat, INI, JSON, XML, and optionally schema output; target existence is conditioned on build components.
sources.applicability: A repository caller/test pattern for metadata/report regressions; does not cover the museum's codecs, channels, or workflow.

sources.title: FFmpeg stack-exhaustion advisory GHSA-rp4v-7m3g-89vg
sources.version_commit: Advisory published 2026-10-08; affected through FFmpeg 9.0.2
sources.locator: Description and references to mov_read_pssh and av_encryption_init_info_free
sources.observed_operation: Opened the advisory and its affected-version/source references.
sources.condition_default_exception: Crafted MP4 with many small PSSH boxes can exhaust stack and consume quadratic CPU in recursive free path; local availability impact, high complexity; advisory identifies versions through 9.0.2.
sources.applicability: Donated files are untrusted parser input. Do not deploy the affected build unchanged; recheck upstream fix/release and isolate parsing. Different crafted files/features may have other risks.

sources.locator: Current stable release and release-series list
sources.observed_operation: Opened current official release index.
sources.condition_default_exception: The index distinguishes stable from development and lists older supported API/ABI-stable series.
sources.applicability: Pin an exact runtime/plugin bundle rather than consume a floating system installation.

sources.title: GstDiscoverer API reference
sources.version_commit: Live official API reference; core Discoverer API is in GStreamer 1.x, with some unrelated page entries marked Since 1.30
sources.locator: GstDiscovererResult; get_result; get_duration; stream info; asynchronous discover_uri/start requirements
sources.observed_operation: Opened and searched API documentation for result, duration, and async behavior.
sources.condition_default_exception: Results separately include URI_INVALID, ERROR, TIMEOUT, BUSY, and MISSING_PLUGINS; missing plugins mean some plugins are missing for full discovery. Async mode needs an iterating GLib main loop/context.
sources.applicability: Good source for per-item error categories and responsive GUI discovery; plugin/build matrix still defines coverage.

sources.title: GStreamer Basic Tutorial 9: Media information gathering
sources.version_commit: Live official tutorial source accessed 2026-10-12
sources.locator: Overview lines on sync vs async; example code's result switch, duration/tags/stream topology; non-OK playback branch
sources.observed_operation: Opened the official tutorial and read its example caller code.
sources.condition_default_exception: Synchronous discover_uri blocks; async is suggested for GUI use. Code logs missing plugins distinctly, then treats any result other than OK as cannot-play.
sources.applicability: A concrete caller example; proposal should improve on its blanket playability message by retaining parse vs preview distinctions.

sources.title: GStreamer Security Advisory 2026-0088
sources.version_commit: Advisory dated 2026-10-08; fixed in gst-plugins-base/good 1.28.8
sources.locator: Summary, affected versions, details, impact, solution
sources.observed_operation: Opened the official project security advisory.
sources.condition_default_exception: Heap out-of-bounds write is through RTP raw-audio depayloaders for crafted SDP/RTSP; base/good <1.28.8 affected; 1.28.8 addresses it.
sources.applicability: The museum's stated local-file route is not this attack path; still use patched plugin bundles and do not enable unnecessary network-source workflows.

sources.condition_default_exception: README distinguishes Good/Great/Excellent, explains feature-flagged formats/codecs and defaults, and describes all-format/all-codec feature flags; status does not guarantee every stream works.
sources.applicability: Rust-native alternative with explicit narrower build profile; support must be selected and tested.

sources.observed_operation: Opened released Cargo.toml source.

sources.applicability: Build default-feature choices materially change input/preview support.

sources.title: Symphonia v0.6.1 release history

sources.observed_operation: Opened the official release and commit-linked notes.
sources.condition_default_exception: Fixes are version-specific; 0.6.1 also changed behavior by fixing conditions and parser hardening but cannot guarantee absence of future defects.
sources.applicability: Demonstrates consequential decoder bug/security fixes; pin reviewed release and regression-test representative media.

sources.title: RFC 8493: The BagIt File Packaging Format
sources.observed_operation: Opened the standards-track informational RFC and read structure/manifest/validity provisions.
sources.condition_default_exception: Payload contents are opaque octet streams; payload manifests list every file; valid means complete with all manifest checksums verified; SHA-256/SHA-512 support required in BagIt 1.0 tools.
sources.applicability: Portable handoff packaging and integrity check without transcoding or changing payload bytes.

sources.title: W3C WCAG 2.2 Understanding Focus Order
sources.version_commit: WCAG 2.2 Understanding document, live W3C WAI page accessed 2026-10-12
sources.locator: SC 2.4.3 and intent/benefits
sources.observed_operation: Opened the W3C WAI Understanding page.
sources.condition_default_exception: When sequential navigation is available and affects meaning/operation, focus order must preserve meaning and operability; visual order need not be identical.
sources.applicability: Keyboard-only validation target for any web/desktop UI, interpreted for the selected native toolkit.

sources.title: W3C WCAG 2.2 Understanding Status Messages
sources.version_commit: WCAG 2.2 Understanding document, live W3C WAI page accessed 2026-10-12
sources.locator: SC 4.1.3, status-message definition, success/error/progress guidance
sources.observed_operation: Opened the W3C WAI Understanding page.
sources.condition_default_exception: For markup-based content, status messages must be programmatically determinable without focus; examples distinguish progress, action result, waiting, and error.
sources.applicability: Accessible textual and assistive-technology announcements for asynchronous batch/review state; validate equivalent behavior in native accessibility APIs.

sources.title: Library of Congress PREMIS tools page: DROID/PRONOM description
sources.version_commit: Live Library of Congress preservation-metadata resource accessed 2026-10-12
sources.locator: DROID paragraph and linked PRONOM description
sources.observed_operation: Opened the Library of Congress tool-description page.
sources.condition_default_exception: Describes DROID as a batch signature-identification tool using PRONOM; identifies format names/version/PUID where possible.
sources.applicability: Optional independent format-identity signal; not a decoder, corruption test, permission source, or proof of preview support.

sources.title: GStreamer audioconvert plugin reference
sources.version_commit: Live plugin reference; audioconvert is in gst-plugins-base, stable series 1.28.8 at access
sources.locator: mix-matrix example; channel reordering for unpositioned inputs; package and raw-audio pad templates
sources.observed_operation: Opened the official GStreamer plugin page and read matrix/reordering examples.
sources.condition_default_exception: The mix matrix explicitly maps input to output channels; unpositioned inputs can be automatically positioned by channel index or forced into a chosen standard layout. This transforms decoded audio in the preview pipeline and can change speaker interpretation.
sources.applicability: Evidence that channel-selective preview is feasible in a decoded pipeline; preserve the original file, do not assume mapping or export the transformed preview as source.

sources.title: SQLite Atomic Commit
sources.version_commit: Live official SQLite technical documentation accessed 2026-10-12
sources.locator: Transaction atomicity after crash/power failure; assumptions about fsync and locks; sections 3, 8, and 9.1
sources.observed_operation: Opened official documentation and searched crash/power-loss and transaction atomicity details.
sources.condition_default_exception: Transactions appear atomic under the documented filesystem/VFS assumptions; broken flush/fsync can undermine it, and documentation warns against using SQLite on network filesystems because locking may be broken.
sources.applicability: Suitable candidate for local per-item resume journal only on local storage with documented durability settings; do not store active job DB on network share.

sources.title: GStreamer Audio Channel Positions
sources.version_commit: Live GStreamer API reference accessed 2026-10-12; channel API includes stable 1.x elements
sources.locator: Channel-mask conversion; channel-position rules; mono/position-less/two-channel no-mask conventions
sources.observed_operation: Opened official audio channel API docs and reviewed channel-position semantics.
sources.condition_default_exception: A channel mask of zero means positions absent; two channels without a mask conventionally imply front-left/front-right in GStreamer audio caps, not speaker identity.
sources.applicability: Do not automatically call left/right channels interviewer/narrator. Preserve raw indices and distinguish technical positions from staff labels.

sources.title: GStreamer Modules
sources.version_commit: Official module index accessed 2026-10-12; stable modules listed as 1.28.8, development 1.29.2
sources.locator: Module table for core, gst-plugins-base, good, ugly, bad, gst-libav, and Cerbero
sources.observed_operation: Opened official module index and reviewed current stable versions and module descriptions.
sources.condition_default_exception: GStreamer is divided into independently versioned modules; many users need core/base/good, while other plugin groups and gst-libav are separate.
sources.applicability: A GStreamer parser/preview capability report must identify each installed module/version, not merely the core runtime.

sources.title: GStreamer Download and platform packaging page
sources.version_commit: Official download page accessed 2026-10-12; page listed 1.28.7 installers while module/release pages listed 1.28.8
sources.locator: Platform installers, toolchain compatibility, Linux/BSD package notes, distribution plugin omissions
sources.observed_operation: Opened official download page and reviewed platform-specific bundle and distribution-package notes.
sources.condition_default_exception: The live page states distributions may split packages or omit bad/ugly/libav plugin modules; at access it still listed 1.28.7 installers, a lag behind the stable module index at 1.28.8.
sources.applicability: A bundle update can lag the framework's stable release; verify the exact platform package includes fixed module versions before relying on its capabilities.
